:::{#exr-bernoulli-hessian-nd}
#### Negative definiteness of the Hessian of a binary sample

In the setting of @exr-bernoulli-hessian-sum,
show that the Hessian $\hess(\prob)$ is negative definite for every $\prob \in (0, 1)$.
Then conclude what it implies for the solution in @thm-bernoulli-score-equation.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-bernoulli-hessian-nd}

A $1 \times 1$ matrix is negative definite exactly when its only entry is negative,
so it is enough to show $\hess(\prob) < 0$.

Fix $\prob \in (0, 1)$. Then:

- $\sqf{\prob} > 0$ and $\sqf{1 - \prob} > 0$;
- $\outbar \ge 0$ and $1 - \outbar \ge 0$, because $\outvar_\iobs \in \cb{0, 1}$;
- $\outbar$ and $1 - \outbar$ are not both zero, because they sum to $1$.

So $\outbar / \sqf{\prob} + (1 - \outbar) / \sqf{1 - \prob}$ is a sum of two nonnegative terms, at least one of them positive.
It is therefore positive, and with $n > 0$:

$$
\hess(\prob) = -n \paren{\frac{\outbar}{\sqf{\prob}} + \frac{1 - \outbar}{\sqf{1 - \prob}}} < 0
$$

This holds for every $\prob \in (0, 1)$,
so $\llik$ is strictly concave on $(0, 1)$.
A strictly concave function has at most one critical point, and it is the maximum.
With $0 < \outbar < 1$, @thm-bernoulli-score-equation says $\outbar$ is that critical point.

:::
